claim.qualifier: Hyundai marketing emphasizes IIHS Top Safety Pick awards, Hyundai's 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty, and J.D. Power-related quality claims for the Ioniq 5.
claim.verbatim_quote: Award-winning Ioniq 5 — IIHS Top Safety Pick+

reality.qualifier: 8 NHTSA recalls in the first year of 2025 Ioniq 5 production. Most concerning: TWO separate high-voltage traction battery recalls (25V482000 and 26V068000). Other recalls: rear floor wiring (25V064000), brake control module on Ioniq 5 N (25V065000, 25V235000 — two campaigns), headlight (25V373000), rear suspension fasteners (25V605000), seat belt retractors (25V797000).
reality.verbatim_quote: Hyundai Motor America is recalling certain 2025 IONIQ 5 vehicles. The high voltage battery [...]; The rear floor wiring [...]; brake control module [...]; seat belt retractors [...].

narrative_one_liner: Hyundai Ioniq 5 2025: 8 NHTSA recalls in first year — including TWO separate high-voltage battery recalls.
narrative: The Hyundai Ioniq 5 2025 is subject to 8 NHTSA recalls in its first model year, the second-highest count in this dataset after Rivian R1S. Two are high-voltage traction battery recalls, which are particularly significant because EV battery packs are extraordinarily expensive to remediate and represent the most safety-sensitive component of an EV. Other recalls include rear floor wiring, brake-control module (twice on Ioniq 5 N variant), headlight, rear suspension fasteners, and seat belt retractors. Hyundai markets the Ioniq 5 with 'award-winning' and 'reliable' language, which is contradicted by this defect-discovery density.
methodology_notes: Tier-1 NHTSA data, authoritative. Two separate battery recalls (25V482000 in 2025 and 26V068000 in 2026) suggest the high-voltage system has accumulated multiple distinct defect modes.
caveats: Two of the brake-control module recalls (25V065000 and 25V235000) apply only to the Ioniq 5 N performance variant, not the SE/SEL trims most buyers select.
Hyundai's IIHS Top Safety Pick+ award is a separate, valid credential about crash performance, not about defect rates. Marketing conflates these dimensions.
Hyundai-Kia EV battery issues have been an industry pattern (recall 25V482000 affected ~150,000 vehicles).
alternative_explanations: Aggressive volume ramp may produce higher recall density without indicating poor underlying engineering.
Hyundai's quality marketing references J.D. Power IQS scores, not NHTSA recall counts; the categories measure different things.
